details:
**Jebel Toubkal**
The highest peak of the Atlas Mountains and of North Africa, at about 4,167 meters, located in the High Atlas roughly 60 kilometers south of Marrakesh. It is the most frequently mentioned peak in questions on the range.

**Aurès Mountains**
The easternmost subrange of the Atlas system, in northeastern Algeria and extending toward Tunisia. Its highest peak is Djebel Chélia, and it is home to the Chaoui Berber people.

**Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia**
The Atlas Mountains stretch about 2,500 kilometers across the Maghreb of northwest Africa through these three countries, running roughly parallel to the Mediterranean coast and separating it from the Sahara.

**Subranges: High, Middle, Anti, Tell, and Saharan Atlas**
The system is divided into several subranges. The High Atlas, Middle Atlas, and Anti-Atlas are in Morocco, while the Tell Atlas runs along the Mediterranean coast and the Saharan Atlas (including the Ksour, Amour, and Ouled Naïl ranges) runs farther inland.

**Berbers (Amazigh)**
The Indigenous people who primarily inhabit the Atlas, speaking Berber languages alongside Arabic. Groups include the Shleuh (Chleuh) of Morocco, the Chaoui of the Aurès, and the Kabyle of Algeria, whose mountain villages were studied by sociologist Pierre Bourdieu.

**Titan Atlas**
The range is named after Atlas, the Titan of Greek mythology condemned to hold up the sky (heavens). Greek legend placed him in northwest Africa.

**Rif Mountains**
A mountain range along Morocco's Mediterranean coast, to the north of the Atlas. It is geologically separate, belonging to the Betic-Rif system tied to Spain, and is separated from the Atlas by the Sebou River valley.

**Marrakesh and Fes**
Moroccan cities in the foothills of the Atlas. Marrakesh, founded by the Berber Almoravid dynasty, lies on the plain north of the High Atlas, within sight of Toubkal.

**Draa River**
A river formed by the joining of the Dadès and Imini rivers, which rise in the High Atlas, flowing south toward the Sahara. The Dadès Gorge is a famous canyon in the range.

**Ouarzazate and the Noor Solar Power Station**
Ouarzazate is a city south of the High Atlas near the Anti-Atlas. Outside it lies the Noor Ouarzazate solar complex, one of the largest concentrated solar power plants in the world.

**Barbary lion and Atlas bear**
The Barbary (Atlas) lion was a lion subspecies of the region, hunted heavily, including by the Romans for gladiatorial games, and now extinct in the wild. The Atlas bear, Africa's only native bear, is extinct.

**Cuvier's gazelle**
A gazelle native to the Atlas Mountains, named for the French naturalist Georges Cuvier. The range is also home to the Atlas cedar and a dwarf viper among the shortest of all vipers.

**Hautes Plaines and chotts**
The High Plateaus (Hautes Plaines) between the Tell Atlas and Saharan Atlas in Algeria contain shallow salt lakes called chotts, such as Chott ech Chergui and Chott el Hodna.

**Grand Erg Occidental**
The "Great Western Erg," a vast sea of sand dunes in the Algerian Sahara just south of the Atlas Mountains.

**Orogeny**
The Atlas were first formed during the Alleghenian (Variscan) orogeny hundreds of millions of years ago. They were later uplifted again during the Alpine orogeny, as Africa collided with Europe and Iberia.
